position: HSG v3 layer = Epistemic Atlas + Structural Theory Transport + Bounded Cross-Domain Donor Search. Sits ABOVE the frozen HSG v1 rung ladder (R0-R7), which sits above HST v1. All three stay canonical at their own scope.
non_finality_doctrine: Operator directive 2026-09-10: if stronger mathematics, cross-domain structure, counterexamples, or new evidence appear, GENERALIZE AND REPLACE the current formulation rather than defend it. Supersession protocol: (1) new evidence never invalidates frozen evidence - HST v1 and HSG v1 lane artifacts are append-only; (2) a replacing formulation ships as a new freeze (v4+) with an explicit supersession chain naming what it generalizes and which frozen results carry over unchanged, which become conditional, and which are refuted; (3) refuted rows keep their counterexample artifacts - a killed theorem is a result, not a loss; (4) defending the current formulation against a stronger one is a defect.

analogy generates PROPOSALS, never warrant; every accepted cross-domain insight becomes theorem/bound/finite certificate/empirical prediction
every donor transfer emits a TheoryTransportV1 receipt (see HSG_V3_DEFINITIONS.md) with preserved/broken/unknown relations + costs
no arbitrary frozen percentages: exploration shares and stopping thresholds calibrated on pilot with recorded sensitivity
false analogies retained and charged - negative outcomes are results (parent absorption, killed theorem, impossibility boundary, equivalence, transferable motif)
parents absorbed, never renamed; unverified parent text marked PARENT_STATEMENT_UNVERIFIED_TEXT

assuming low rank of the relevance matrix R[a,d] instead of measuring it
retroactively upgrading the evidence class of pre-freeze lanes with post-freeze discoveries
treating the Higgs->optimizer calibration donor as evidence rather than as a calibration case
defending v3 against a stronger formulation instead of superseding it

hostile.instance: Two donors {A,B}, one target lemma: A supplies a technique, B an invariant, each alone worthless (f=0,0), together sufficient (f({A,B})=1). Marginal of B rises 0->1 after reading A.
hostile.kills: Adaptive submodularity (increasing marginal) and with it the greedy 1-1/e-style / log-competitive guarantee; parent guarantee invalid in this configuration, requiring joint set-level search or pair-as-item re-registration.

Sviridenko 2004, A note on maximizing a submodular set function subject to a knapsack constraint, Operations Research Letters 32(1)

hostile.instance: 1-D bandit X=[0,1], dissimilarity l=|x-y|, f=1/2 on [0,1-delta], f(1)=1: the single optimum sits at maximal distance from the broad mediocre shelf; any Lipschitz constant valid across the jump (nu>=1/(2delta)) makes optimism vacuous, any shelf-fit constant makes the bound invalid at x=1. The optimum shares a hidden structural attribute with the target (Higgs-style donor) that l does not measure.
hostile.kills: The chosen dissimilarity l (and any router/hierarchical tree built on it), i.e. the validity of the local-Lipschitz assumption under l - NOT the existence of remote analogy and not the parent theorem, which conditions on a correct dissimilarity.

hostile.instance: K=2 donors, one elimination round: donor A has small value epsilon visible at any depth; donor B* has true value 1 but its depth-r estimate is 0 for all r < d* (signal only at full reconstruction depth). Round 1 runs at depth d1 < d*, SH keeps the top 1 arm = A, B* is discarded deterministically for any halving schedule that does not reach d* before elimination.
hostile.kills: The premise that the best arm is separated the right way at every resource level SH reaches (registered-model applicability of SH to late-blooming donors), not the parent theorem itself.
